article.Citation/Title: Krupitsky, E. M., Burakov, A. M., Dunaevsky, I. V., Romanova, T. N., Slavina, T. Y., & Grinenko, A. Y. (2007). Single versus repeated sessions of ketamine-assisted psychotherapy for people with heroin dependence. Journal of Psychoactive Drugs, 39(1), 13-19.
article.InterventionDescription: Ketamine 2.0 mg/kg IM for ketamine-assisted psychotherapy (KPT), 1.5-2 hr sessions; single session vs. three monthly sessions with addiction counseling; inpatient/outpatient at a St. Petersburg hospital.

ae_events.Description: Acute increase in systolic and (particularly) diastolic blood pressure of 20-30% during the ketamine psychotherapy session.

article.Outcome: Primary outcome per Methods ('the rate of abstinence was considered the primary outcome variable') and Results ('Retention in Treatment and Abstinence Rate'): 13/26 (50%) abstinent at 1-year follow-up in the multiple-KPT group vs 6/27 (22.2%) in the single-KPT group. Reported as two-group proportions because no single numeric effect-size statistic accompanies this comparison.
article.SD: No dispersion or test-statistic value is printed for the abstinence-rate comparison itself; the Kaplan-Meier survival analysis is described narratively only. Figure 1's caption shows 'P<O.Ol' (read as P<0.01) for the overall survival curve while the text reports '(p < 0.05)' for the same endpoint (13/26 vs 6/27) — an internal inconsistency, flagged rather than silently reconciled per the non-fabrication rule. Coded '.' since no statistic (e.g., a log-rank value with df) accompanies either p-value.
article.PVal: Text states '(p < 0.05)' immediately after reporting 13/26 (50%) vs 6/27 (22.2%) abstinence (Results). Figure 1's caption instead prints a discrepant 'P<0.01' for what appears to be the same survival comparison. Recorded the text's threshold, '<0.05', since it is directly attached to the proportions used for Outcome; the figure's discrepant value is noted here, not resolved or averaged.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: 53 = 26 (multiple-KPT) + 27 (single-KPT), the full randomized cohort analyzed for the 1-year abstinence comparison (Results). The 6 participants who relapsed and dropped out before randomization (after the first, pre-randomization KPT session) are excluded from this N; participants who later relapsed/dropped out within the randomized groups remain in the 26/27 denominators as treatment failures, consistent with the survival-analysis framing.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: 13 of 14 criteria met; only sample_size_power is absent — no a priori or post hoc power calculation or sample-size justification appears anywhere in Methods or Results.

article.Comparator: Both arms received active ketamine-assisted psychotherapy; the comparison is a session-frequency (dose-analogous) design — one KPT session vs. three monthly KPT sessions — not a placebo or no-treatment control (Design). Per codebook, a dose-comparison design counts as Comparator = 1.
article.BaseStatus: No explicit mild/moderate/severe label is given. Coded 'Severe' as a clearly inferable judgment: participants were hospitalized inpatients undergoing detoxification for ICD-10/DSM-IV heroin dependence present ≥1 year, with mean dependence duration 38.8±30.4 months (Participants) — a chronic, hospitalization-requiring presentation.
article.ConfoundYN: Authors explicitly compared the randomized groups on age, duration of heroin abuse, and gender and reported 'no statistically significant differences' (Results) — a substantive discussion/check of potential confounders across arms, though not a statistical adjustment within the outcome model.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Recruited from a real inpatient addiction-treatment hospital (Participants: 'Leningrad Regional Center of Addictions, a 300-bed hospital'), but extensive exclusion criteria (psychiatric comorbidity, other SUDs, significant medical illness, pending legal charges, concurrent treatment elsewhere) screened out a substantial share of the eligible clinical population (73 screened, 59 enrolled), so coded 0.
article.Retention (%): 42/53 completed the assigned treatment protocol: 4/26 (15.4%) dropped from the multiple-KPT group after session 2, and 7/27 (25.9%) dropped from the single-KPT group after the first counseling session (Results). 42/53 x 100 = 79.2%. Denominator is the randomized N (53) per rule. This value falls within 2 points of 80, per the prompt's explicit flag requirement.
article.PercentFem: 10 females of 59 enrolled (Participants: '49 males and 10 females') = 16.9%.
article.QualityOfLifeMeasured: The Purpose-in-Life Test (PLT) assesses existential meaning/purpose (Frankl-based), not a standard quality-of-life instrument (e.g., no SF-36/WHOQOL analog is used); coded 0.
article.ReductionMeasured: Substance-use outcomes are reported as binary abstinent/relapsed via physical exam, urine screens and TLFB (Treatment Assessment; Results); no distinct partial-reduction or harm-reduction endpoint separate from abstinence/relapse/cessation is reported.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: St. Petersburg / Leningrad Region, Russia (Participants; author affiliations).
article.NParticipantsWithAE / AE_denominator: Side Effects section states the blood-pressure increase was 'noted in all participants' without giving a separate numeric safety-population count. Interpreted as the full enrolled cohort who received at least one ketamine session (n=59), since this side effect was observed before the post-first-session randomization split. Flagged as an inference from 'all participants' rather than an explicitly printed count.
article.ArmScope: All 59 enrolled participants received at least one ketamine session before randomization, and the reported blood-pressure effect is described for 'all participants' with no non-exposed comparator arm anywhere in the study (both randomized groups are ketamine-exposed); coded psychedelic_arm.

ae_events.Krupitsky 2007_AE01: Acute systolic/diastolic BP elevation (20-30%) during ketamine dosing is described as transient and occurring only during the session, with no mention of pharmacological intervention or persistence beyond the dosing period (Side Effects: 'An anesthesiologist was available throughout all ketamine sessions to treat any possible complications' — standby only, not used for this event). Graded Mild per the rubric's explicit 'transient mild BP/HR elevation' example; SeverityIndeterminate = N because the magnitude, timing, and absence of intervention are all stated. SeveritySource = rubric because the authors did not assign a CTCAE grade or SAE label to this event. NAffected = 59 reflects the article's 'noted in all participants' language, interpreted as the full ketamine-exposed enrolled cohort (see AE_denominator rationale above); this is an inference, not a printed count.

config_proposal.note: 1-year abstinence was 13/26 (50%) multiple-KPT vs 6/27 (22.2%) single-KPT (text p<0.05; Figure 1 caption prints a discrepant P<0.01 for the same comparison, unresolved). OR computed from the 2x2 abstinent/relapsed table as (13x21)/(13x6) = 3.5, favoring the multiple-session arm. The study's actual reported test was a Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with no printed log-rank statistic, so this OR is an approximation of the final-timepoint proportions rather than a direct conversion of an author-reported effect size.
